proposal: The Mandate criticizes career staff for reserving excessive numbers of key policy positions as career reserved, for dominating Senior Executive Service personnel evaluation boards where noncareer executives were expected to lead, and for career executive training that underplays the political role in leadership. The implied recommendation (framed as criticism with an expectation) is that noncareer officials lead SES evaluation boards, that career-reserved designations be limited, and that training reflect political leadership of the bureaucracy.

status_summary: A presidential memorandum dated 2025-01-20 directed agencies to reconstitute Executive Resources Boards with senior noncareer chairs and a noncareer majority, and to reconstitute Performance Review Board membership with people committed to fully enforcing SES performance evaluations. OPM memos of February 2025, as summarized by CRS, asked agencies to request redesignation of career-reserved CIO positions as general (2025-02-04) and directed a general review of SES positions while encouraging conversion of career-reserved positions to general (2025-02-05 and 2025-02-24); CRS gives no count of positions actually converted. An OPM memo of 2025-05-29 set noncareer chairs and majorities for Executive Resources Boards, replaced the Executive Core Qualifications, and announced an 80-hour program covering executive orders and constitutional foundations; Executive Order 14207 (signed 2025-02-10) directed elimination of the Federal Executive Institute, and OPM launched executive development programs on 2025-08-06. Performance Review Boards remain subject to a statutory career majority for career executives, and OPM's SES performance rule (effective 2025-10-15) only encourages members committed to the appraisal system.

timeline.event: Presidential memorandum directed agencies to reconstitute Executive Resources Boards with senior noncareer chairs and a noncareer majority, and to reconstitute Performance Review Board membership with individuals committed to full enforcement of SES performance evaluations.
OPM memo asked agencies to request that OPM redesignate career-reserved SES CIO positions as general (as summarized by CRS).
OPM memo directed a general review of SES positions and encouraged converting career-reserved positions to general; a further memo of 2025-02-24 did the same (as summarized by CRS).
Executive Order 14207 directed OPM to take steps to eliminate the Federal Executive Institute, a federal leadership-training program (published 2025-02-14).

OPM memo required noncareer chairs and noncareer majorities on Executive Resources Boards, replaced the Executive Core Qualifications, called for political leadership involvement in SES hiring, and announced new executive training.
OPM announced two executive development programs aligned with the new Executive Core Qualifications and the administration's priorities.
OPM published a final SES performance appraisal rule (effective 2025-10-15) encouraging Performance Review Board members committed to applying the appraisal system.
OPM published a final rule on SES Candidate Development Programs (effective 2026-07-27) requiring OPM approval of agency programs and tying them to the Executive Core Qualifications.

title: Shift SES boards, career-reserved posts and training toward political leadership
uncertainties: The February 2025 OPM memos were read only through the CRS summary; CRS says the actions would result in redesignating some career-reserved positions but gives no count, and no OPM approval records were found. A Federal Register notice listing positions career reserved during 2024 (published 2025-05-20) exists, but its table was not compared with earlier years, and no notice for 2025 was found. Whether the new ECQs and training reduce the underplaying of political leadership cannot be measured; OPM itself describes the training as aligned with administration priorities. CRS does not discuss the Federal Executive Institute.
